items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Monopoly"?
items.answer: A market with a single seller of a product that has no close substitute, with barriers to entry.
items.markingKey: (b) Monopoly: A market with a single seller of a product that has no close substitute, with barriers to entry.
options: A market with a very large number of buyers and sellers of an identical product, where no single firm can influence the price.
A market with a single seller of a product that has no close substitute, with barriers to entry.
A market with many sellers of differentiated products, such as brands of soap or restaurants.
A set of buyers and sellers of a product, and the arrangements through which they exchange it.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of monopoly but not of perfect competition?
items.answer: Number of sellers: one seller
items.markingKey: (c) monopoly: Number of sellers: one seller. The other options describe perfect competition.
options: Number of sellers: a very large number of sellers
Control over price: no single seller can influence the price

items.stem: Which of the following statements about markets and market structures is NOT correct?
items.answer: Online markets are not markets.
items.markingKey: (d) Incorrect statement: Online markets are not markets.
options: An oligopoly has a few large sellers.
Perfect competition has a very large number of sellers.

items.stem: Hundreds of farmers sell the same variety of wheat in a large mandi, and none can change the price. Which market structure is described?
items.answer: Perfect competition
items.markingKey: (c) Perfect competition. Many sellers of an identical product.

items.stem:
A handicraft seller in Varanasi has moved from a weekly local fair to selling across India and abroad on an online marketplace.
(i) Classify both markets on the basis of area and mode of transaction. (ii) State one advantage of the change.
items.answer: (i) Local and physical market; national/international and online market. (ii) Wider customer base; sales at any time; lower cost of reaching distant buyers (any one).
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Local and physical market; national/international and online market. (ii) Wider customer base; sales at any time; lower cost of reaching distant buyers (any one).

items.stem:
Diya plans to open a café in Agra, where there are already many cafés, each with its own style, menu and loyal customers. Her cousin wants to sell rice in a large wholesale market where hundreds of traders sell the same variety at one price.
(i) Identify the market structure each will face. (ii) What should Diya do to succeed? (iii) Can the cousin charge a higher price?
items.answer: (i) Diya: monopolistic competition (many sellers, differentiated products); cousin: perfect competition (many sellers, identical product, uniform price). (ii) Differentiate the café (theme, menu, service) and promote the brand. (iii) No; under perfect competition one price prevails and buyers will go elsewhere.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Diya: monopolistic competition (many sellers, differentiated products); cousin: perfect competition (many sellers, identical product, uniform price). (ii) Differentiate the café (theme, menu, service) and promote the brand. (iii) No; under perfect competition one price prevails and buyers will go elsewhere.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Dozens of brands of toothpaste compete with different flavours and claims. (a) Which market structure is described? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Monopolistic competition (b) Many sellers with product differentiation.
items.markingKey: (a) Monopolistic competition, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Many sellers with product differentiation.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A monopolist faces many close competitors.
Reason (R): A monopolist is the single seller of a product with no close substitute.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about markets and market structures is correct?
items.answer: A monopolist is the single seller of a product.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: A monopolist is the single seller of a product.
options: Products are differentiated under perfect competition.
A monopolist is the single seller of a product.
A monopoly has many sellers of identical products.

items.stem:

(i) Identify the market structure each will face. (ii) What should Tara do to succeed? (iii) Can the cousin charge a higher price?
items.answer: (i) Tara: monopolistic competition (many sellers, differentiated products); cousin: perfect competition (many sellers, identical product, uniform price). (ii) Differentiate the café (theme, menu, service) and promote the brand. (iii) No; under perfect competition one price prevails and buyers will go elsewhere.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Tara: monopolistic competition (many sellers, differentiated products); cousin: perfect competition (many sellers, identical product, uniform price). items.stem: State any three methods of collecting primary data.
items.answer: Survey; Personal interview; Observation; Focus group discussion; Test marketing
items.markingKey: Any three of: Survey; Personal interview; Observation; Focus group discussion; Test marketing (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain "Focus group discussion" with reference to the methods of collecting primary data.
items.answer: Focus group discussion: A guided discussion with a small group of target customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: A guided discussion with a small group of target customers.

items.stem: Differentiate between primary data and secondary data with reference to suitability and cost and time.
items.answer: (i) Suitability: primary data: collected for the specific purpose, so highly suitable; secondary data: may not fully suit the present purpose. (ii) Cost and time: primary data: more costly and time-consuming; secondary data: cheaper and quicker.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Suitability: primary data: collected for the specific purpose, so highly suitable; secondary data: may not fully suit the present purpose. (ii) Cost and time: primary data: more costly and time-consuming; secondary data: cheaper and quicker.

items.stem: Yash stood in a supermarket for a week noting which juice brands shoppers picked up first. Which method of market research is being used?
items.answer: Observation
items.markingKey: (b) Observation. Customer behaviour is watched.

items.stem:
Priya has little money and wants to know how many households in her town might buy solar water heaters.
(i) Suggest one source of secondary data and one primary method. (ii) Why start with secondary data?
items.answer: (i) Census or government reports / electricity board data; a small survey of households. (ii) It is cheaper and quicker.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (i) Census or government reports / electricity board data; a small survey of households. (ii) It is cheaper and quicker.

items.stem: Farhan gave a printed set of ten questions to 300 college students in Dehradun about their snack habits. Which method of market research is being used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Survey. A sample is asked a set of questions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Survey; 2 marks for the justification: A sample is asked a set of questions.

items.stem:
Lakshmi wants to launch a protein drink for gym-goers in Lucknow. She first reads industry reports on the health-drink market, then asks 200 gym members to fill in a short form, watches what members buy at gym counters, and finally sells the drink in two gyms for a month.
(i) Identify the market research methods used. (ii) State one advantage and one limitation of primary data.
items.answer: (i) Secondary data (industry reports); survey (form filled by 200 members); observation (watching purchases); test marketing (two gyms for a month). (ii) Advantage – suited to the purpose and current; limitation – costly and time-consuming.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Secondary data (industry reports); survey (form filled by 200 members); observation (watching purchases); test marketing (two gyms for a month). (ii) Advantage – suited to the purpose and current; limitation – costly and time-consuming.

items.stem: Explain any five sources of secondary data.
items.answer: (i) Census and government reports: Population, income and industry data. (ii) Trade journals and magazines: Information on industry trends. (iii) Websites and online databases: Data on competitors and markets. (iv) Reports of industry associations: Statistics and studies of an industry. (v) Company records: Past sales and customer records of the firm itself.
items.markingKey: Any five points, 1 mark each (point with a line of explanation): (i) Census and government reports: Population, income and industry data. (ii) Trade journals and magazines: Information on industry trends. (iii) Websites and online databases: Data on competitors and markets. (iv) Reports of industry associations: Statistics and studies of an industry. (v) Company records: Past sales and customer records of the firm itself.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Saanvi gave a printed set of ten questions to 300 college students in Mumbai about their snack habits. (a) Which method of market research is being used? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Survey (b) A sample is asked a set of questions.
items.markingKey: (a) Survey, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: A sample is asked a set of questions.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "Data already collected by others, such as census reports, government publications, trade journals and websites."
items.answer: Secondary data
items.markingKey: (b) Secondary data: Data already collected by others, such as census reports, government publications, trade journals and websites.

items.stem: Aditya invited eight young mothers to discuss what they want in a baby-food brand, with him guiding the discussion. Which method of market research is being used?
items.answer: Focus group discussion
items.markingKey: (c) Focus group discussion. A small group discusses with a moderator.

items.stem: Distinguish between primary data and secondary data on the basis of cost and time, source and suitability.
items.answer: (i) Cost and time: primary data: more costly and time-consuming; secondary data: cheaper and quicker. (ii) Source: primary data: collected first-hand by the researcher; secondary data: already collected by others. (iii) Suitability: primary data: collected for the specific purpose, so highly suitable; secondary data: may not fully suit the present purpose.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Cost and time: primary data: more costly and time-consuming; secondary data: cheaper and quicker. (ii) Source: primary data: collected first-hand by the researcher; secondary data: already collected by others. (iii) Suitability: primary data: collected for the specific purpose, so highly suitable; secondary data: may not fully suit the present purpose.

items.stem: What is meant by "Market segmentation"?
items.answer: Dividing a market into distinct groups of customers with similar needs, characteristics or behaviour.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Dividing a market into distinct groups of customers with similar needs, characteristics or behaviour.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of segmentation but not of positioning?
items.answer: Order: done first
items.markingKey: (a) segmentation: Order: done first. The other options describe positioning.
options: Focus: the product as perceived by customers
Meaning: creating an image of the product in customers' minds
Order: done after choosing the target segment

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A customer persona helps in designing the product.
Reason (R): It describes the needs, habits and problems of a typical customer.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Kapoor Brothers makes a separate range of shoes for children aged 5 to 12. Which basis of segmentation is used?
items.answer: Demographic
items.markingKey: (b) Demographic. Age is used.

items.stem: Read the situation and answer. Iyer Enterprises makes a separate range of shoes for children aged 5 to 12. (a) Which basis of segmentation is used? (b) Give one reason in support of your answer.
items.answer: (a) Demographic (b) Age is used.
items.markingKey: (a) Demographic, 1 mark; (b) reason, 1 mark: Age is used.

items.stem:
Diya plans a range of healthy tiffin meals in Agra. She imagines a typical customer: "Riya, 28, software engineer, lives alone, works long hours, wants low-oil home-style food, orders through apps." She will serve only young working professionals and advertise the meals as 'Ghar ka khana, office pe'.
(i) What is the description of Riya called, and why is it useful? (ii) Identify the bases of segmentation used. (iii) Identify the targeting strategy and the positioning.
items.answer: (i) Customer persona; it helps design the product, price and promotion for real needs. (ii) Demographic (age, occupation); psychographic or behavioural (lifestyle, ordering habit). (iii) Concentrated (niche) marketing to young professionals; positioned as home-style food delivered at the office.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) Customer persona; it helps design the product, price and promotion for real needs. (ii) Demographic (age, occupation); psychographic or behavioural (lifestyle, ordering habit). (iii) Concentrated (niche) marketing to young professionals; positioned as home-style food delivered at the office.

items.answer: Customer persona

items.stem: State any three goals of marketing for an enterprise.
items.answer: Creating awareness; Increasing sales and market share; Building the brand; Customer satisfaction and loyalty; Earning profit
items.markingKey: Any three of: Creating awareness; Increasing sales and market share; Building the brand; Customer satisfaction and loyalty; Earning profit (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain "Earning profit" with reference to the goals of marketing for an enterprise.
items.answer: Earning profit: Covering costs and earning a return.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Covering costs and earning a return.

items.stem:

items.answer: A is true, but R is false.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Iyer Enterprises starts selling its pickles through an online marketplace. Which element of the marketing mix is involved? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Place. It concerns the channel of distribution.

items.stem:
Riya runs a small yoga studio in Patna. She has trained, friendly instructors, offers online booking, a calm and clean studio, monthly plans at ₹1,200, and promotes the studio on social media.
(i) Identify five elements of the marketing mix in the case.
items.answer: (i) People: friendly instructors; process: online booking; physical evidence: calm, clean studio; price: ₹1,200 monthly plans; promotion: social media (product: yoga classes).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) People: friendly instructors; process: online booking; physical evidence: calm, clean studio; price: ₹1,200 monthly plans; promotion: social media (product: yoga classes).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about marketing for an enterprise is correct?
items.answer: The four Ps are product, price, place and promotion.

Physical evidence is one of the original four Ps.
The four Ps are product, price, place and promotion.
Marketing begins only after the product is sold.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about market research is NOT correct?
items.answer: Market research is done only after the business fails.
items.markingKey: (d) Incorrect statement: Market research is done only after the business fails.
options: Census reports are a source of secondary data.
Market research is done only after the business fails.

items.stem: Thakur Enterprises calls customers after every repair to check that they are satisfied. Which goal of marketing is being pursued?
items.answer: Customer satisfaction and loyalty
items.markingKey: (a) Customer satisfaction and loyalty. It ensures satisfaction.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about segmentation, targeting and positioning is NOT correct?
items.answer: Targeting means dividing the market into segments.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: Targeting means dividing the market into segments.
options: A customer persona is a profile of a typical customer.
Targeting means dividing the market into segments.
Age and income are demographic bases.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Primary data"?
items.answer: Data collected first-hand by the researcher for a specific purpose, such as through surveys or interviews.
items.markingKey: (a) Primary data: Data collected first-hand by the researcher for a specific purpose, such as through surveys or interviews.
options: Data collected first-hand by the researcher for a specific purpose, such as through surveys or interviews.
A small group of people led by a moderator in a discussion about a product or idea.
A set of written questions used to collect information from respondents.
The systematic collection and analysis of information about customers, competitors and the market to support business decisions.

items.stem: Many restaurants in Dehradun each offer their own menu, ambience and brand. Which market structure is described? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Monopolistic competition. Many sellers of differentiated products.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Monopolistic competition; 2 marks for the justification: Many sellers of differentiated products.

items.stem:
Manish runs a small yoga studio in Patna. He has trained, friendly instructors, offers online booking, a calm and clean studio, monthly plans at ₹1,200, and promotes the studio on social media.
(i) Identify five elements of the marketing mix in the case.
items.answer: (i) People: friendly instructors; process: online booking; physical evidence: calm, clean studio; price: ₹1,200 monthly plans; promotion: social media (product: yoga classes).
items.markingKey: 5 marks: (i) People: friendly instructors; process: online booking; physical evidence: calm, clean studio; price: ₹1,200 monthly plans; promotion: social media (product: yoga classes).

items.stem: Explain "Undifferentiated marketing" with reference to the targeting strategies.
items.answer: Undifferentiated marketing: One offer for the whole market.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: One offer for the whole market.

items.stem: Manish stood in a supermarket for a week noting which juice brands shoppers picked up first. Which method of market research is being used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Observation. Customer behaviour is watched.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Observation; 2 marks for the justification: Customer behaviour is watched.

items.stem: Explain "Trade journals and magazines" with reference to the sources of secondary data.
items.answer: Trade journals and magazines: Information on industry trends.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Information on industry trends.
